day_shape: 56 items: Netanyahu ties war's end to regime fall or nuclear halt, IDF announces killing of Hamas UAV commander Hamam Eid plus two others, Iran-Russia FM call and Tasnim claim of tanker mine strike in Hormuz, heavy Khamenei/Defa Press 'revenge' cycle; nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Iran war pause and mediation tracks
threads.summary: Netanyahu told media the Iran war ends only when the regime falls or abandons its nuclear programme, while a senior Iranian source told Reuters Tehran will hold fire so long as US strikes remain paused. Jerusalem Post reported the US and Iran have submitted responses to a Pakistan-Qatar proposal to resume talks, and Russia's Vienna envoy said suspending attack plans is insufficient.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz security and shipping
threads.summary: Iran's parliament National Security Commission began reviewing a strategic action plan for Hormuz security drawn from 12 proposals, and Hormozgan Corps announced controlled explosions east of Bandar Abbas Monday morning. IRGC-linked Tasnim claimed a tanker exploded after hitting a naval mine in the Strait, while Jerusalem Post reported Iran-Oman progress on navigation arrangements.

threads.label: IDF strikes on Hamas operatives in Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF announced the killing of Hamam Eid, commander of Hamas's UAV cell in central Gaza, in a strike the previous day, and separately confirmed the deaths of weapons-production official Fares al-Masri and Nukhba operative Muhammad Abu Shakyan. Jerusalem Post also reported a Sunday strike in Deir al-Balah killed a senior Hamas-run internal security officer.

threads.label: Khamenei 'martyred leader' messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted an excerpt from the Supreme Leader's 18 July funeral message declaring 'revenge is the demand of our nation and must certainly take place'. Defa Press and IRIB carried a pledge-renewal ceremony for media managers, a Qalibaf condolence message to Salami's widow, and the Islamic Propaganda Organisation head's remarks on 'the blood of Shahid Khamenei'.

threads.label: Regime claims on US and Israeli setbacks
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB published matched items listing 'America's very heavy losses' from Iranian attacks and claiming Trump is 'pleading' to return to a 60-day ceasefire, citing US commentator David Pyne. Defa Press also cited a New York Times account of Trump's 'strategic impasse' and former Israeli general Haliva conceding miscalculation of Iran's missile arsenal, plus a claimed 30TB cyber leak from Israeli defence supplier IMCO.

events.summary_en: The head of the Islamic Propaganda Organisation, emphasising that 'the world must know we will not abandon the blood of Shahid Khamenei', said: in the school of Ahl al-Bayt, seeking justice does not mean vengeance, but rather a life-giving act to preserve truth, open hearts, and continue the path of guardianship. events.title_en: Azhei: 26 billion euros resolved in the field of currency obligations — Head of Judiciary
events.summary_en: As a result of the entry and follow-up by the judiciary, from December of last year to now, seven and a half billion euros have been used to clear currency obligations. Furthermore, 26 billion euros have also been resolved in this field. Additionally, criminal cases have been opened for 300 people, including officials and non-officials. As a result of the judiciary's diligent follow-up, more than 3,000 people who held rented commercial cards have been identified. These rented commercial cards can be a source of corruption. We have held the responsible sectors in this field, including the Central Bank, the Ministry of Industry and Mines, accountable.

events.summary_en: The Hebrew media Israel Hayom reported a major cyber attack against IMCO, one of the suppliers of the Zionist regime's defence industries. Simultaneously, the 'Cyber Support Front' group announced that by publishing information on LeakForum, they gained access to 30 terabytes of this company's data and released part of it. According to the released information, the extracted data includes technical documents, production blueprints, contracts, internal correspondence, employee information and data related to military projects and systems including the Iron Dome. events.title: Two more Hamas operatives were killed in Israeli strikes in the Gaza Strip last week, the military announces. According to the IDF, one strike in the Strip's north on Tuesday killed Fares al-Masri, a commander in Hamas's weapons production division. The military says al-Masri was involved in "the production of weapons as part of Hamas's efforts to rebuild its capabilities, in violation of the ceasefire agreement." Another strike in northern Gaza on Tuesday killed Mohammad Abu Shakian, a member of Hamas's elite Nukhba Force, according to the IDF. The IDF says both operatives worked to advance attacks on troops and Israeli civilians, and they were killed to "remove the threat."
